q: Which pairing correctly gives an example of a basic activity of daily living (ADL) and an instrumental activity of daily living (IADL)?
o: ADL: preparing a meal; IADL: bathing oneself
ADL: bathing oneself; IADL: preparing a meal
ADL: gait-speed testing; IADL: grip-strength testing
ADL: joint-range testing; IADL: muscle-strength testing
explanation:
Basic activities of daily living (ADLs) are personal care tasks. Instrumental activities of daily living (IADLs) are the more complex tasks needed to manage a household and live independently in the community.

**Bathing oneself is a basic ADL and preparing a meal is an IADL. Eating and organizing the food one will eat are distinct tasks.**

**A. Meal preparation as basic and bathing as instrumental.** This switches the categories. Cooking requires planning and household skills, while washing the body is personal care.
**B. Bathing as basic and meal preparation as instrumental.** This separates self-care from the activities needed to run one’s day at home.
**C. Gait speed and grip strength.** These tests measure walking performance and muscle strength. Neither describes a daily activity carried out for oneself.
**D. Joint range and muscle strength.** These measurements can help explain why dressing or cooking is difficult. They measure impairments rather than either class of daily task.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 820, 1571.

q: When discussing surgery for benign prostatic enlargement, what technical advantage does bipolar transurethral resection have over monopolar resection?
o: Hypotonic irrigation fluid reduces the sodium load during resection
Isotonic irrigation fluid reduces the risk of TURP syndrome
Isotonic irrigation fluid increases free-water absorption during resection
Hypotonic irrigation fluid reduces the risk of electrolyte disturbances
explanation:
Bipolar TURP can use **isotonic saline irrigation**, lowering the risk of the dilutional hyponatremia of classic TURP syndrome.

**A. Hypotonic irrigation fluid reduces the sodium load during resection.** The advantage is the ability to avoid hypotonic irrigation.
**B. Isotonic irrigation fluid reduces the risk of TURP syndrome.** Saline absorption supplies much less electrolyte-free water than hypotonic nonconductive irrigants, although fluid overload remains possible.
**C. Isotonic irrigation fluid increases free-water absorption during resection.** Isotonic saline does not cause the proposed greater free-water load.
**D. Hypotonic irrigation fluid reduces the risk of electrolyte disturbances.** Absorption of hypotonic fluid increases the risk of electrolyte disturbances.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 568.

q: גבר בן 79 עם mild cognitive impairment, יתר לחץ דם, ו-CKD stage 3a (eGFR 48) עומד לשחרור לאחר תיקון hip fracture. הוא גר לבד בבית דו-קומתי. הפיזיותרפיסט מדווח שהוא זקוק ל-contact guard לביצוע transfers ומפגין בלבול קל לגבי hip precautions. בנו יכול לבקר פעמיים בשבוע. התרופות כוללות lisinopril 10 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg, ו-oxycodone 5 mg q6h PRN. איזו disposition לשחרור מאזנת בצורה הטובה ביותר בין צרכי ההחלמה שלו לשמירה על עצמאות?
o: שחרור הביתה עם outpatient PT
העברה למוסד שיקום subacute
רישום לתכנית PACE עם נוכחות ב-day center
בית עם מטפל פרטי 24 שעות
explanation:
אחרי שבר ירך השאלה המיידית היא מי יהיה ליד המטופל בכל מעבר ובעלייה במדרגות. PACE יכולה לתאם שיקום ועזרה בקהילה רק כאשר אפשר לבנות סידור בטוח גם מחוץ לשעות המרכז.
**PACE עם מרכז יום היא האפשרות המשולבת לטווח הארוך, בתנאי שנמצאו זכאות ותמיכה בטוחה בבית. אם אין עזרה במעברים, יש לשקול שיקום תת־חריף לפני החזרה הביתה.**

**א. פיזיותרפיה במרפאה.** היא דורשת הגעה ואינה מספקת אדם שיסייע בכל מעבר בבית.
**ב. שיקום תת־חריף.** זו חלופה מתאימה בפועל אם עדיין נדרשת עזרה פיזית והבית אינו בטוח לשחרור.
**ג. PACE ומרכז יום.** הצוות עשוי להסדיר שיקום, הסעות וסיוע בבית. נוכחות במרכז לבדה אינה עונה על הצורך בלילה.
**ד. מטפל פרטי בכל שעות היממה.** זו אפשרות לעזרה פיזית אם יש מימון, אך לבדה אינה מסדירה מקצועות שיקום ומעקב.

אסמכתא · Hazzard 8e, עמ׳ 238–240, טבלה 17-1. Medicare, PACE, Who can get PACE?
Key note: הרשמה ל־PACE מחייבת יכולת לחיות בבטחה בקהילה בעזרת התוכנית. למטופל דרושה השגחה פיזית במעברים ולא מתוארת עזרה זמינה בבית בין ביקורי הבן. בנסיבות אלה שיקום תת־חריף הוא אפשרות בטוחה לשחרור המיידי.
ref: Hazzard Ch 17 — COMMUNITY-BASED LONG-TERM SERVICES AND SUPPORT, AND HOME-BASED MEDICAL CARE

q: An older adult with malnutrition has both reduced muscle mass and reduced muscle function. Which interpretation does Hazzard describe as the usual scenario?
o: Sarcopenia caused by the existing malnutrition
Reduced muscle mass with preserved muscle function
Malnutrition occurring without impairment of muscle
Sarcopenia indicating an adequate nutritional state
explanation:
Low intake can first reduce muscle quantity and, as tissue and strength decline, can also impair function. **When both are reduced in a malnourished person, malnutrition causing secondary sarcopenia is a common explanation.**

**A. Malnutrition causing sarcopenia** Existing nutritional depletion plus functional loss makes the two diagnoses compatible. Look for additional contributors as well.
**B. Low mass with preserved function** This pattern can favor malnutrition alone, but the patient's muscle function is already reduced.
**C. Malnutrition without muscle impairment** Some patients may have malnutrition without muscle loss. Here both mass and function are abnormal.
**D. Sarcopenia implying adequate nutrition** Sarcopenia says nothing about adequate intake. Nutritional deficiency is one of its potentially treatable causes.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 736, Differential Diagnosis.
ref: Hazzard Ch 49 — MUSCLE AGING AND SARCOPENIA

q: A 72-year-old woman has severe depression, reduced food intake and function, and limited response to several medication trials. Electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) is being considered. Which information is consistent with Hazzard?
o: Older adults tend to respond less well than younger patients
Trials have found medication more effective than this treatment
Its initial benefits remain durable without maintenance treatment
It warrants early consideration after limited medication response
explanation:
Electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) uses a controlled electrical stimulus under anesthesia to treat severe depression. Loss of intake and function makes it important to consider an effective intervention without a prolonged sequence of further drug trials.
**Consider ECT early for severe depression with limited medication response.**

**A. Older adults respond less well.** Older patients often respond at least as well as younger adults and may respond particularly well.
**B. Medication is more effective.** Comparative treatment evidence favors ECT for severe depression. Most studies of acute ECT reported response rates above 80%, although response need not mean full remission.
**C. Initial benefit persists automatically.** Relapse can follow an acute course. Discuss continuation medication, psychotherapy or maintenance ECT as appropriate.
**D. Consider ECT now.** Several unsuccessful trials plus deteriorating intake justify specialist assessment, including medical and anesthetic suitability and her treatment preferences.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1014 · American Psychiatric Association, What Is Electroconvulsive Therapy?

q: A woman with fibromyalgia and depressive symptoms asks what duloxetine may contribute. Which combination of effects is described in Hazzard?
o: Improvement in pain and depression, with improved quality of life
Improvement in pain, with worse depression and reduced quality of life
Improvement in depression, with worse pain and reduced quality of life
Improvement in quality of life, with unchanged pain and depression
explanation:
Duloxetine inhibits serotonin and norepinephrine reuptake and has both analgesic and antidepressant effects. In a woman with fibromyalgia and depressive symptoms, **pain, mood, and quality of life may all improve**.

**A. Improvement in all three domains.** Less widespread pain and fewer depressive symptoms can each make daily activities easier.
**B. Less pain but worse depression.** Duloxetine also treats depression, so worsening mood is not the expected therapeutic effect.
**C. Better mood but worse pain.** Serotonin and norepinephrine help regulate pain signaling, giving duloxetine an analgesic role in fibromyalgia itself.
**D. Better quality of life alone.** Pain and mood are direct treatment targets. Assess both alongside how well the patient functions day to day.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1647.
ref: Hazzard Ch 103 — FIBROMYALGIA AND MYOFASCIAL PAIN SYNDROMES

q: A woman with COPD remains breathless at rest despite optimal treatment of her lung disease. Which principle applies to drug treatment of refractory dyspnea according to Hazzard?
o: Consider replacing lung-disease treatment with an opioid for symptom relief
Consider selecting an opioid without accounting for cognitive changes
Consider an opioid for symptom relief while monitoring adverse effects
Consider selecting morphine without accounting for impaired kidney function
explanation:
Refractory dyspnea persists despite appropriate treatment of the underlying illness. **An individualized opioid trial may relieve symptoms, with monitoring for cognitive and other adverse effects**.

**A. Replace COPD treatment.** Continue beneficial cause-directed care while adding symptom relief.
**B. Ignore cognition.** Sedation or confusion may outweigh relief for the individual.
**C. Monitor a symptom trial.** Assess perceived breathlessness, alertness and tolerability.
**D. Ignore kidney impairment.** Morphine metabolites can accumulate, altering the choice or dose.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1074.
ref: Hazzard Ch 69 — MANAGEMENT OF COMMON NONPAIN SYMPTOMS

q: A woman with heart failure and preserved ejection fraction has pulmonary congestion and is receiving a diuretic. Which principle should guide adjustment of treatment intensity?
o: Increase diuresis until relative hypotension develops
Relieve congestion while avoiding excessive diuresis
Reduce diuresis in order to maintain pulmonary congestion
Titrate diuresis to produce a fall in cardiac output
explanation:
Elevated filling pressure causes pulmonary congestion in HFpEF, yet forward flow still depends on adequate filling volume. **Titrate the diuretic to relieve congestion without producing volume depletion**.

**A. Aim for relative hypotension** Falling pressure can signal that preload and output are now too low.
**B. Relieve congestion cautiously** Follow dyspnea, weight, edema, renal function and orthostatic symptoms as the dose changes.
**C. Preserve congestion** Persistently high pulmonary venous pressure prolongs breathlessness.
**D. Target lower output** Reduced forward flow threatens kidney and tissue perfusion and is an adverse effect of overdiuresis.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1186.

q: A woman with hypernatremia is hemodynamically stable and requires correction of a water deficit. Which principle should guide treatment?
o: Replace water while adjusting treatment and monitoring serum sodium
Prescribe a fixed water volume based on the initial calculation
Restrict water as the main means of lowering serum sodium
Use isotonic saline as the main means of replacing free water
explanation:
A stable patient with hypernatremia needs replacement of missing water. **Estimate the deficit, replace water and adjust to serial sodium values and ongoing losses**.

**A. Monitored water replacement.** The response shows whether the estimated deficit and loss rate were accurate.
**B. Fixed calculated volume.** A calculation cannot anticipate changing intake, renal losses or ongoing illness.
**C. Restrict water.** This increases the water deficit and can worsen hypertonicity.
**D. Isotonic saline as principal replacement.** Use it first when circulation is threatened. A stable water deficit requires water or a suitable hypotonic fluid.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 588.
ref: Hazzard Ch 39 — SYSTEMS PHYSIOLOGY OF AGING AND SELECTED DISORDERS OF HOMEOSTASIS

q: An 82-year-old man with peripheral arterial disease has a heel pressure injury covered by dry, stable eschar, without purulence or sepsis. What needs to be assessed before deciding on debridement?
o: Eschar thickness to choose a debridement instrument
Arterial perfusion to assess healing after debridement
Dressing type to begin an autolytic debridement method
Wound duration to schedule repeat debridement sessions
explanation:
Debriding an ischemic heel can turn dry stable necrosis into an open wound with inadequate blood flow for healing. The absence of purulence or sepsis reduces the urgency for source control.

**Assess arterial perfusion and protect the dry, stable heel eschar.** Offload the heel, monitor for instability or infection and seek vascular assessment as indicated.

**A. Measure eschar thickness.** Thickness does not tell whether the patient's arterial supply could support healing after excision.
**B. Assess arterial supply.** Adequate perfusion is a prerequisite to elective debridement of a lower-limb wound. Stable ischemic eschar is left intact.
**C. Select an autolytic dressing.** Softening the eschar before assessing perfusion can remove its protective cover.
**D. Use duration to schedule repeat debridement.** Chronicity alone is not an indication to cut into a poorly perfused heel.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 688–689, 696, Figures 46-1 and 46-2.

q: Does isolated CLL leukocytosis mandate treatment?
o: Yes - mature circulating CLL lymphocytes generally produce leukostasis that warrants treatment
No - isolated leukocytosis without other treatment indications does not require therapy
No - symptomatic CLL progression is generally managed without disease-directed therapeutic intervention
Yes - the absolute lymphocyte count outweighs its rate of increase in treatment decisions
explanation:
Isolated CLL lymphocytosis can be observed when there is no symptomatic or progressive disease. **A high count alone does not mandate treatment**.

**A. Mature cells cause leukostasis.** Leukostasis is uncommon with the small, mature lymphocytes of CLL.
**B. Observe isolated leukocytosis.** Monitor trends, symptoms, adenopathy and cytopenias to identify evolving treatment indications.
**C. Observe symptomatic progression routinely.** Disease-related symptoms or progressive cytopenias can warrant treatment.
**D. Absolute count overrides growth rate.** Rapid change can provide more information about disease activity than a single count.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1491.

q: Does a high postvoid residual consistently predict symptomatic UTI?
o: Yes - prospective studies generally confirmed increased symptomatic UTI with high residuals
Yes - a high residual is generally sufficient evidence of symptomatic urinary infection
No - the cited case-control study found a lower frequency of high residuals in recurrent UTI
No - prospective studies did not consistently find an association
explanation:
A postvoid residual measures urine remaining after voiding. **Prospective studies did not consistently find that a high residual predicts symptomatic UTI.**

**A. Yes - prospective studies generally confirmed increased symptomatic UTI with high residuals.** An association in some observations was not consistently reproduced during prospective follow-up.
**B. Yes - a high residual is generally sufficient evidence of symptomatic urinary infection.** Retention can occur without infection. Diagnosing UTI requires compatible clinical findings.
**C. No - the cited case-control study found a lower frequency of high residuals in recurrent UTI.** The case-control observation went in the other direction, with high residuals more frequent among women with recurrent infection.
**D. No - prospective studies did not consistently find an association.** Distinguishing an observed association from consistent prospective prediction avoids treating a bladder-scan result as infection.

Reference · Hazzard 8e (marked), pp. 1702.

q:
בת 78, מאושפזת במחלקה פנימית, מתלוננת על כאבים באזור פי הטבעת ושלשולים מימיים מזה יומיים. סימנים חיוניים תקינים. בבדיקת הבטן – בטן רכה, לא רגישה. בבדיקות המעבדה ללא עליית מדדי דלקת, עליה קלה בתפקודי כליה. בדיקות צואה שליליות לפרזיטים וקלוסטרידיום.
מה השלב הבא בבירור?
o: בדיקה רקטלית
קולונוסקופיה
בדיקת CT בטן
תרבית צואה חוזרת
keySource: IMA 2024-Sep Basic official answer key after appeals, Q105
explanation:
Watery leakage can pass around retained hard stool and mimic infectious diarrhea. In this older patient with rectal symptoms, **perform a digital rectal examination** to identify a potentially reversible impaction.

**A. Rectal examination.** A bedside examination can detect a hard mass and directly change management.
**B. Colonoscopy.** Endoscopy can be needed for persistent or concerning symptoms, but it is not the first way to identify an accessible stool plug.
**C. Abdominal CT.** CT is useful when complications or proximal disease are suspected. It need not precede a focused bedside assessment.
**D. Repeat stool culture.** Another stool culture would not address overflow from impaction.

Reference · Harrison 22e, pp. 305–306.
